sinks.name: DMSG
sinks.reason: Typical debug logging function takes a string or format and data to print; logging can leak sensitive data or be used to inject format specifiers.

sinks.name: DMSG
sinks.reason: Additional arguments provided to a debug print could contain sensitive values that are formatted into output.

sinks.name: IMSG
sinks.reason: Name suggests 'I Message' or incoming message; first parameter often holds data payload read/processed by the function

sinks.name: IMSG
sinks.reason: Second parameter commonly represents size of the message buffer, important for bounds and parsing

sinks.name: IMSG
sinks.reason: Additional parameter likely indicates message type, flags, or routing info that affects security-relevant handling

sinks.name: TEE_MemCompare
sinks.reason: Likely pointer to memory whose contents are read for comparison; comparing secrets can leak information or be targeted in timing attacks.

sinks.name: TEE_MemCompare
sinks.reason: Likely pointer to memory whose contents are read for comparison; same risks as buffer A.

sinks.name: TEE_MemCompare
sinks.reason: Controls number of bytes compared; using incorrect or attacker-controlled length can cause over-read or reveal partial data.

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove
sinks.reason: Data is written into this buffer; may overwrite sensitive data or be used later

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove
sinks.reason: Data is read from this buffer; may contain sensitive input that is copied

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove
sinks.reason: Controls amount of data moved; incorrect value can cause overflows or truncated sensitive data

sinks.name: snprintf
sinks.reason: receives formatted data written by the function; may be used later in security-sensitive contexts (e.g., constructing commands, tokens)

sinks.name: snprintf
sinks.reason: controls maximum written bytes; incorrect use can lead to truncation or off-by-one issues affecting security

sinks.name: snprintf
sinks.reason: determines how subsequent arguments are interpreted; if attacker-controlled, can lead to format-string vulnerabilities or disclosure

sinks.name: strcmp
sinks.reason: Contains user or external data being read and compared; content can influence control flow or authentication checks

sinks.name: strcmp
sinks.reason: Contains user, external, or secret string being read and compared; comparison result may leak or validate sensitive data

sinks.name: strlen
sinks.reason: strlen walks the buffer to determine length and therefore reads the contents; if the buffer is attacker-controlled or untrusted, its contents and termination affect control flow and can reveal sensitive information or cause out-of-bounds reads.
